title: Bhimtal & Sattal near Nainital. Discover boating, birdwatching, history, best time to visit, things to do, nearby attractions, and travel tips.
content:
About Bhimtal,

Bhimtal, located about 22 km from Nainital, is a serene and spacious lake destination, larger and quieter than Naini Lake. Surrounded by beautiful hills, Bhimtal is known for its beautiful island in the middle of the lake, which houses an aquarium. Legend says the lake is named after Bhima from the Mahabharata, adding a touch of mythology to its charm.

The calm waters make Bhimtal a perfect spot for boating, kayaking, and paddle boating, while the nearby temples and walking trails give visitors both spiritual and nature-filled experiences. Unlike the bustling Nainital, Bhimtal offers peace and fewer crowds, making it ideal for families and couples looking for a relaxing getaway.

About Sattal,

Just 5 km from Bhimtal, Sattal (meaning Seven Lakes) is a natural wonder. Surrounded by thick pine and oak forests, this destination consists of a cluster of seven interconnected freshwater lakes. Each lake has its own unique charm and is home to migratory birds, butterflies, and rich flora.

Sattal is especially loved by nature lovers, birdwatchers, and photographers. It’s also a hub for camping and adventure activities like kayaking, angling, and trekking. Its untouched natural beauty makes it feel more rustic and offbeat compared to Bhimtal and Nainital.

Best Time to Visit:

  • March - June (Peak Season): Pleasant weather (15°C - 25°C), best for boating and birdwatching.
  • September - November (Moderate Season): Clear skies (10°C - 20°C), great for nature walks and camping.
  • December - February (Low Season): Cold months (4°C - 12°C), peaceful for those who enjoy winters and misty lake views.

Distance from City Center:

  • Bhimtal: 22 km from Mall Road, Nainital.
  • Sattal: 27 km from Mall Road, Nainital.

Timings & Entry Fee:

  • Timings: Open all day.
  • Entry Fee: Free, but boating and activities are chargeable.

Things to Do in Bhimtal & Sattal:

  • Enjoy boating, kayaking, and paddling in Bhimtal Lake.
  • Visit the aquarium on Bhimtal’s island.
  • Explore ancient Bhimeshwar Mahadev Temple near Bhimtal.
  • Go birdwatching in Sattal, home to over 500 bird species.
  • Experience butterfly watching at Sattal’s Butterfly Museum.
  • Try camping, trekking, or angling at Sattal.
  • Capture beautiful photographs of lakes and forests.
  • Taste local snacks from nearby stalls.

Best 10 Places to Visit Near Bhimtal & Sattal (within 50 km):

1- Naini Lake (22–27 km): Heart of Nainital with boating.

2- Naina Devi Temple (22–27 km): Sacred Shakti Peeth.

3- Snow View Point (24–29 km): Famous for Himalayan views.

4- Tiffin Top (26–31 km): Picnic spot with panoramic views.

5- Naina Peak (28–33 km): Highest trekking point in Nainital.

6- Hanuman Garhi Temple (25–30 km): Sunset point with large Hanuman idol.

7- Khurpatal Lake (14–19 km): Quiet lake for picnics and angling.

8- Ghorakhal Temple (12–15 km): Wish-fulfilling temple with bells.

9- Eco Cave Gardens (23–28 km): Fun caves and family outing spot.

10- Sariyatal Lake (20–25 km): A small, picturesque lake surrounded by gardens.
excerpt: Bhimtal & Sattal are two of the most beautiful lakes near Nainital, offering a mix of mythology, nature, and adventure. While Bhimtal charms with its island and boating activities, Sattal attracts those who love wilderness, camping, and birdwatching.
